label: Compliance manager, FS, 9y, NO warm network (graceful-failure test)

questionnaire.Q3b: Mid-size UK retail bank, second-line compliance monitoring team.
questionnaire.Q4: Governance and compliance; monitoring, regulatory change implementation, and control testing.
questionnaire.Q6: Rebuilt the consumer-duty monitoring framework from scratch after the 2023 FCA rules landed — mapped 40+ controls to outcomes, built the testing calendar, and got it through internal audit with no findings.
questionnaire.Q7: Occasionally junior colleagues ask me how to read a new regulation, but it stays inside my team. I have never advised anyone outside my employer.
questionnaire.Q8: Thorough, calm with regulators, good at turning vague rules into concrete controls.
questionnaire.Q11: I have only ever worked inside one bank. I know retail-banking compliance well but I genuinely don't know how firms buy external compliance help, or who decides.
questionnaire.Q13: Weak. Maybe 12 LinkedIn connections, almost all current colleagues. I have no contacts who own budgets and no one I could call about independent work without it feeling cold and odd.

hook_insight_must_reference: a structural / platform / professional-body access route to first clients (because the user has no warm network to lean on)
the consumer-duty monitoring depth from Q6, not generic 'compliance experience'
hook_insight_must_not_be: anything that assumes a warm network of budget-holders the user can contact (Q13 is empty and Q12 is null — this is the failure mode being tested)
'reach out to your network' framing in any form
generic 'experienced compliance professional ready to go independent' framing
expected_outputs.graceful_failure_expectations: The plan must NOT depend on the user contacting a warm network. First moves should be structural (register on a compliance-contractor platform / marketplace), visibility (a focused LinkedIn point of view), or community (join a named compliance practitioner community and contribute) — never 'message 15 people you know'. Income outlook and pacing must reflect a cold start with no network and low independence confidence.
expected_outputs.commercially_distinctive_one_liner: Consumer-duty monitoring specialist who must reach a cold market through platforms and visibility, not a warm referral network.

grading_notes: EDGE COHORT (Battery 1, 2026-06-01). Tests D9 graceful failure for the networkless user — the biggest substance risk in the AI pre-pass. Bevan: review expected_outputs, especially first_move_must_not_be_type and graceful_failure_expectations, before locking.

label: Transformation/PMO manager, 10y, based in Toronto (non-UK leakage test)

questionnaire.Q3b: Canadian arm of a global management consultancy; large-scale operating-model and systems transformations for financial-services and public-sector clients.
questionnaire.Q4: Project delivery and consulting; programme leadership and operating-model design.
questionnaire.Q6: Led a 14-month core-banking migration PMO for a Canadian credit union — 60-person programme, brought it in on time after a troubled start by rebuilding the delivery governance and stage-gating.
questionnaire.Q7: Yes — peers across Toronto consulting ask me to sanity-check troubled-programme recovery plans, maybe monthly.
questionnaire.Q8: Calm in delivery crises, strong at programme governance, trusted to take over when a programme is going sideways.
questionnaire.Q11: Canadian financial-services and public-sector organisations running large change programmes. They buy recovery and assurance help from the big consultancies, but increasingly want independent senior operators who cost less and embed faster.
questionnaire.Q12: One independent programme-assurance review for a former colleague's firm last year, paid, three weeks.
questionnaire.Q13: Strong across Toronto and Canadian FS consulting.

hook_insight_must_reference: the troubled-programme recovery / assurance angle from Q6 (the distinctive wedge)
the Canadian / Toronto market the user named in Q11 and Q15
hook_insight_must_not_be: anything UK-specific (IR35, Companies House, HMRC, 'sole trader vs Ltd', GBP pricing) applied to a Canadian-based user
expected_outputs.graceful_failure_expectations: The product is UK-first by default (bible §23). For a non-UK user it must EITHER localise (Canadian market framing, CAD pricing, no UK-only tax/legal references) OR clearly flag that guidance is UK-centred and may not apply. The failure mode is silently applying UK pricing benchmarks, IR35, and Companies House steps to a Toronto user as if they were facts.
expected_outputs.commercially_distinctive_one_liner: Toronto-based troubled-programme recovery specialist — must be served in a Canadian market frame, not a silently-UK one.

grading_notes: EDGE COHORT (Battery 1). Tests whether UK-first assumptions leak into a non-UK user's market snapshot, pricing, and guidance. Bevan: decide the intended behaviour (localise vs honestly flag) and encode it in graceful_failure_expectations before locking.

label: Data analyst, 3y, below the ICP experience floor (over-promise test)

questionnaire.Q3b: Series-B SaaS scale-up, central data team.
questionnaire.Q4: Analysis and reporting; dashboards, SQL, some experimentation analysis.
questionnaire.Q6: Built the self-serve revenue dashboard the whole commercial team now uses; cut ad-hoc data requests to the team by about half.
questionnaire.Q7: Not really — I'm usually the one asking for advice.
questionnaire.Q8: Fast with SQL, good at turning a vague question into a clean dashboard.
questionnaire.Q11: I've only worked at this one start-up. I don't really know how companies buy external data help.

hook_insight_must_reference: an honest, achievable entry point given only 3 years' experience and no network
hook_insight_must_not_be: senior / fractional-leadership pricing or positioning the user cannot credibly command at 3 years
any implication that an independent income could realistically replace their salary soon
expected_outputs.graceful_failure_expectations: The ICP is 5-12 years (bible §5). At 3 years the product should be HONEST about limited track record and weak commercial readiness — temper pricing, lengthen time-to-revenue, and avoid senior framing. The failure mode is selling this user the same confident senior-independent story as a 12-year manager. Acceptable to recommend a modest project-based entry; not acceptable to over-promise.
expected_outputs.commercially_distinctive_one_liner: Early-career analyst who should be told the honest, modest version — not sold a senior-independent fantasy.

grading_notes: EDGE COHORT (Battery 1). Below-ICP boundary case. Tests honesty / over-promise control (D2). Open question for Bevan: should the funnel even take this user's money, or fit-gate them? Encode the decision before locking.

label: Blended ops/data/product lead, 12y, no clean archetype (rationale-reasoning test)

questionnaire.Q1: Head of Service Operations (also owns the data and product-ops functions)
questionnaire.Q3b: UK healthtech scale-up; I run service operations, the ops-analytics team, and product-operations — the role was stitched together over three reorgs.
questionnaire.Q4: Operations and process, plus analytics, plus some product delivery — genuinely split across all three.
questionnaire.Q6: Designed and stood up the patient-onboarding operating model end-to-end: the service blueprint, the ops-analytics that monitor it, and the product backlog that automates it. Cut onboarding time from 9 days to under 2.
questionnaire.Q7: Constantly — founders and heads of ops at other healthtechs ask me how to join up service design, ops data, and product. It is the thing people think I'm unusually good at.
questionnaire.Q8: Joining up the bits nobody else connects: service, data, and product as one system.
questionnaire.Q11: UK healthtech and regulated-service scale-ups. They struggle because service design, data, and product sit in separate silos and nobody owns the join. They buy point specialists and end up with a disconnected mess.
questionnaire.Q12: Two paid advisory days for a former colleague's healthtech, helping them design their onboarding ops model.
questionnaire.Q13: Strong across UK healthtech founders and ops leaders.

expected_outputs.primary_archetype_label: any defensible closest match (Service Design / Ops / Analytics)
hook_insight_must_reference: the cross-silo join (service + data + product) that is the user's genuine distinctive edge from Q6/Q8/Q11
hook_insight_must_not_be: a flattening of the blended profile into one generic single-discipline label (e.g. plain 'operations consultant') that loses the join
expected_outputs.rationale_must_reason_not_restate: The recommendation rationale must EXPLAIN why the chosen path fits this blended profile — naming the cross-silo wedge as the differentiator and why a single-discipline option would be weaker. It must not simply restate the user's selection or list the strands. This is the exact own-goal the AI pre-pass caught on report 773a2230.
expected_outputs.graceful_failure_expectations: An ambiguous profile must be handled per bible §13 ('most don't fit cleanly; returns closest match plus two nearest alternatives; report reflects the blend'). The failure mode is forcing the user into one ill-fitting archetype and producing a recommendation that ignores their actual cross-functional edge.
expected_outputs.commercially_distinctive_one_liner: Cross-silo service+data+product operator whose value IS the join — the recommendation must reason about the blend, not flatten it.

grading_notes: EDGE COHORT (Battery 1). Tests classifier behaviour on a genuinely blended role AND recommendation-rationale quality (judge-6). Directly targets the restate-not-reason own-goal from the pre-pass.
